## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-fascicle *pìyù* (譬喻 = *avadāna* / *dṛṣṭānta*, "parable") anthology of some 11 short narratives, attributed in the Chinese canon to [支婁迦讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E5%A9%81%E8%BF%A6%E8%AE%96) Lokakṣema. Signature: 「後漢月支沙門支婁迦讖譯」.

**Abstract**

T204 is one of three closely-related *Zá pìyù jīng* anthologies in the Taishō (T204, [T205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0062), [T207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0064)), all titled identically but distinguished by attribution: T204 to Lokakṣema (Hàn), [T205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0062) anonymous Hàn-register, [T207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0064) compiled by [道略](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E7%95%A5) Dàoluè (Latter-Qín). Modern scholarship (Mizuno; Nattier) is sceptical of the attribution of T204 to Lokakṣema: the linguistic register and content are inconsistent with Lokakṣema's better-attested Mahāyāna translations and the work is more likely a slightly later compilation that was retrospectively attached to his name in catalog tradition. The bracket 178–200 reflects Lokakṣema's documented active period at Luòyáng if the attribution is accepted.

The *Zá pìyù jīng* anthologies as a group are foundational sources for the East-Asian Buddhist *pìyù* genre — short *exempla* narratives used for popular preaching — and influenced the development of Chinese Buddhist popular literature.
